macula_hebrew_cherith_surface_english_20.label: MACULA exact Hebrew morph surfaces with Cherith English definitions
macula_hebrew_cherith_surface_english_20.declared_from: The entry's own structure, read across all 43,304 routes on 15,871 keys. In 43,304 of 43,304 rows the route is the whole definition, character for character: each record is one contextual English gloss for one Hebrew surface, with no head, no rendering list and no notes, so no mark's meaning depends on a region. 40,992 routes carry no mark at all. The provider writes no comma and no semicolon anywhere (route 0, definition 0). Its closed set is 11 marks, 2,360 occurrences; every occurrence falls in exactly one of 24 shapes; 0 unexplained. Exactly one mark, '/', divides readings in meaning, once, and it is not separated (see its entry).

regions.note: Every route is its whole definition, so the provider has one region.

~.means: a gap inside one English phrase: the place where English carried by another Hebrew word or morph of the verse stands ('bring ~ back' is 'bring [him] back'). Never a boundary between two readings.
~.evidence: 171 of the 1,871 routes carrying '~' have a sibling route on the same key that is the same text with the gap closed (e.g. השב: bring ~ back | bring back; השב: put ~ back | put back); the word after the gap is a verbal particle (out, up, down, away, back and the like) in 668 of them; in 11 does each side stand as a route of its own on the same key.
~.falsifier: A '~' whose two sides are two alternative renderings rather than two halves of one phrase. Searched as: each side stands as a route of its own on the same key. 11 today, and each reads as one phrase split around its gap, not as two alternatives: correlative frames, phrasal verbs, a noun phrase (עם: as ~ as; פן: that ~ not; ישב: put ~ back; ישב: brought ~ back; ישב: brought ~ again; גם: both ~ and; נערה: young ~ woman; מ: so that ~ not; דבר: what ~ say; דבר: what ~ said; תחתי: in ~ place). Also a '~' mid-route without a space on both sides: 0 today.

’.means: the apostrophe of English spelling inside one word: possessive ’s, plural possessive s’, contracted n’t
’.evidence: אתנ: donkey’s | דד: uncle’s | מררי: Merari’s | נשרים: eagles’ | בנ: sons’ | אם: don’t
’.falsifier: A '’' with no letter before it (an opening quotation mark): 0 today.

-.means: joins two parts into one English word or one name (father-in-law, one-fifth, beth-arabah, Esh-baal); once, at the head, it writes the gloss as a bound suffix (-self)
-.evidence: ערבה: beth-arabah | אשרים: daughter of-cypresses | חיים: life-giving | חתנ: father-in-law | בד: -self
-.falsifier: A '-' with a space on either side (a dash standing between two glosses): 0 today.

!.means: the gloss's own mood, imperative or exclamation, at the end of the one reading
!.evidence: שא: count! | לו: now! | מי: if only! | הבו: love !
!.falsifier: A '!' anywhere but the last character, which would end one gloss and begin another: 0 '!' or '?' today.

?.means: the gloss is interrogative; at the end of the one reading
?.evidence: מתי: how? | ו: he? | ה: not? | מה: for why ?
?.falsifier: As for '!': a '?' anywhere but the last character.

(.means: an annotation or a supplied word inside one reading, never a scope over alternatives: a lexicon number tying a name-part to its compound name, a number equation standing where the gloss would, or English supplied for sense
(.evidence: numbers shared by the halves of one name: 1127 on בן: Ben (1127) and גבר: Geber (1127); 1128 on דקר: Deker (1128) and בן: Ben (1128). Supplied English: ו: or (against ) | הוא: he (found) | מעל: (just) above | פני: face of (him)
(.falsifier: A parenthesis holding a comma, a slash or any mark but '=' and '+' (a scope over alternatives): 0 today. Unbalanced parentheses: 0 today.

).means: closes the annotation or supplied word

=.means: inside a number equation only: the entry on the left is composed of the entries on the right
=.falsifier: An '=' outside a parenthesis of numbers: 0 today.

+.means: inside a number equation only: joins the component entry numbers. This is not Strong's KJV '+' (a word supplied by the translators); the provider never writes '+' beside English
+.falsifier: A '+' outside a parenthesis of numbers (e.g. before an English word, as Strong's writes it): 0 today.

..means: once, a full stop glued to the head of 'and', with nothing before it in the field: it ends nothing the route holds, so it divides nothing. Whether it is a stray or the end of the preceding English sentence carried onto the conjunction, one instance cannot say.
..falsifier: A '.' with words on both sides of it (a sentence boundary inside one field): 0 today.

/.means: alternation between two renderings of one head that share the words after them: 'thumbs/big toes of' is 'thumbs of' or 'big toes of'
/.rule: Not separated. A cut at the slash keeps both pieces and each is the provider's run, but the first piece, 'thumbs', loses the 'of' the provider wrote once for both; printing 'thumbs of' would join pieces the provider never wrote together, which is a derivation. Held whole until the owner rules (open question).
/.falsifier: A second '/' route whose pieces each stand alone as complete glosses; then the slash is a plain separator and the rule can be written from more than one instance.

macula_hebrew_cherith_surface_english_20.precedence_note: No mark separates in this provider, so no order arises. If the owner rules the single '/' a separator, it is the only one and stands alone.
macula_hebrew_cherith_surface_english_20.closure: The mark set above is closed. A route carrying any mark not listed (a comma or a semicolon included) is reported and ships whole.
macula_hebrew_cherith_surface_english_20.separates_on_note: Every route ships whole. That is the default for an undeclared provider too; what this declaration adds is the closed set, the meanings, and the record that the provider writes one reading per field: 43,304 of 43,304 routes are their whole definition, no field carries a comma or a semicolon, and the one mark that divides in meaning (the '/', 1 route) shares a tail across its alternatives.
macula_hebrew_cherith_surface_english_20.not_done_here: No gap is filled: '~' is never replaced by the English it stands for, since that English belongs to another word's record. No supplied-word parenthesis is stripped and no lexicon number is removed. The provider's run-together words (e.g. 'havetrodden', 'toanger', 'greatamount', several after a '~') are its own spelling and are not respaced here.
